name: DomeGallery-TS-TW
title: DomeGallery
description: Dozens of rounded photo tiles wrap around a virtual sphere that fills the view. Dragging turns the ball of images with momentum, and clicking one tile enlarges it toward the middle.
use: A portfolio or campaign wants an immersive, browsable wall of images instead of a flat grid.
avoid: It needs a sized parent and many image downloads, and the drag is pointer-only.
a11y: Tiles are labelled buttons and Escape closes the viewer, but Enter or Space never opens a tile and no focus ring is drawn. (keyboard: partial, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Many small rounded-square photos, all greyscale, sit in a curved grid over a black stage, forming the front of a large sphere. The outer edges fade into darkness while the centre stays sharp and dense.
behaves: Dragging spins the sphere sideways, with only a small vertical tilt allowed, and momentum carries it after release. Clicking a tile expands that photo toward the centre over a dimmed backdrop.
customise: Images, fit basis, radius bounds, segment count, grayscale, blur colour, drag feel and the opened image size and radius are props.
weight: heavy: A 3D sphere of about two hundred image tiles that all re-transform together while it spins.
demo: Twelve Unsplash portraits and lifestyle photos, repeated across the sphere and shown in grayscale.
issues: All photos are forced to greyscale by default, which hides the colour of the imagery.
Only a fixed number of tile slots exist, so a larger image set is partly dropped with a console warning.
polishWhy: Immersive and coherent with a smooth edge fade, though the grey wash flattens every photo.
